q: What will read as a defect on this run under shop lights?
right: The metal clips and black pads still on the faces.
wrong: The color change from magenta to red.

q: What's wrong on this panel?
right: Only the top is stuck. The rest of the field is wrinkled and loose.
wrong: Rivets are tented along a seam.

q: What is standing against the orange panel at the door?
right: A folding ladder, set right at the door.
wrong: A film roll on a stand.

q: Graphic is seated. What's left before you call it done?
right: Pull the nose tape low and slow, then check the rivet line and wheel-well edge.
wrong: Post-heat the whole graphic again to be safe.

q: Fix order at this marker light?
right: Lift the fingers, glass toward the housing, then cut the light out.
wrong: Cut the light out first, then chase the fingers.

q: What's wrong with this nose panel?
right: It's hung, not glassed. The crown seam is open and the lower edge is loose.
wrong: It's glassed but the film is scorched.

q: Where does the cut go on this door handle?
right: Into the black voids, off the paint, leaving a tuck the housing can hide.
wrong: Straight across the face of the scoop.

q: Why check this satin hood in raking light?
right: Satin shows every finger. No gloss reflection hides them.
wrong: Satin can't take a relief cut.

q: Why the felt edge on this printed film?
right: It keeps the printed grain from getting scratched.
wrong: It heats the film as it goes.

q: Next move on this hatch?
right: Glass the broad hatch, then feed up to the chrome. No bridge over the bar.
wrong: Stretch over the chrome bar now and trim later.

q: How do you finish this inside corner?
right: Glass each wall, then tuck the corner.
wrong: Stretch one sheet across the inside angle.

q: How do you wrap these slats?
right: Each slat on its own.
wrong: One sheet stretched across all the openings.

q: The torch is on the floor. When does it come up?
right: After the nose panel is down, and only per the film TDS.
wrong: Now, to relax the salmon panel before it's registered.

q: The face is glassed. What still needs work?
right: The raw plywood inside the round holes. Wrap or tuck each edge.
wrong: The QR code needs a relief cut.

q: Next move on this RV side?
right: Move the ladder instead of overreaching. Hinge the panel, then glass it.
wrong: Climb with the full sheet and stretch it on.

q: Where does this blade stay?
right: On the edge, cutting the waste. Not back into the finished face.
wrong: Back into the face to square it up.

q: Next move on this cut?
right: Relax the bunch, cut on a flat path, and snap a fresh blade if it drags.
wrong: Keep sawing through the gather.

q: Where does this knife stay?
right: In the corner, off the show face, with the white wall as the guide.
wrong: Out on the show face for a straighter line.

q: What has to happen before this blade touches the film?
right: Clean off the drop and the specks.
wrong: Nothing. Cut right through them.

q: What's the rule on this peel?
right: Keep it low. Stop if the pink layer under it starts to lift.
wrong: Pull straight up, fast.

q: Next move in this box?
right: Move the can, glass the sheet to the walls, then wrap or trim the bare plywood rim.
wrong: Leave the rim bare. It's inside the box.

q: Move on these finger rows?
right: Lift a finger and chase it out.
wrong: Squeegee them flat, hard.
